newsitem.title: ITALY: League withdraws Italy broadcast bill amendments.
newsitem.headline: League withdraws Italy broadcast bill amendments.

text.p: Italy's separatist Northern League party said on Tuesday it had decided to withdraw almost all the amendments it had presented to a draft bill on setting up a watchdog for the broadcasting and communications sector.
League senator Roberto Castelli told reporters of the party's decision after a meeting with Post and Communications Minister Antonio Macccanico.
The bill is already being examined by the Senate (upper house). Of the 3,300 amendments to the bill presented, 3,100 were submitted by the League.

Castelli said that the League would withdraw all but around 15 amendments, making it more likely that the government will now not have to call a confidence vote to ram the bill onto the statute books.
Approval of the bill is a precondition for the privatisation of state telecoms holding Stet.
